title: GCP Pub/Sub: `subscriptionSize` is removed — the scaler refuses the trigger

detection.reason: checked on the ScaledObject/ScaledJob triggers the agent projects (trigger type + metadata KEY names, never values) — a key supplied through a TriggerAuthentication or an environment variable is not a metadata key and is not scanned

quote: **GCP PubSub Scaler**: The `subscriptionSize` setting is DEPRECATED and is removed in v2.20 - Use `mode` and `value` instead (#7720)
remediation: The tag flips to `deprecated=` at v2.20.0 and the parser rejects a trigger that still sets `subscriptionSize` — every gcp-pubsub trigger named stops scaling after the hop. Replace it with `mode: SubscriptionSize` + `value` before upgrading.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh,scaledjobs.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.triggers[]? | select((.type == "gcp-pubsub") and (.metadata // {} | has("subscriptionSize"))) | "\($o.kind) \($o.metadata.namespace // "-")/\($o.metadata.name) trigger=\(.type)"'  # each row is refused by the 2.20 scaler

title: IBM MQ: the `tls` setting's code is deleted — a trigger that 2.18 refused scales again

detection.reason: checked on the ScaledObject/ScaledJob triggers the agent projects (trigger type + metadata KEY names, never values) — a key supplied through a TriggerAuthentication or an environment variable is not a metadata key and is not scanned

quote: **IBM MQ Scaler**: The `tls` setting code is removed (#6094)

title: Cron trigger: metric names for comma-separated cron expressions change

detection.reason: the cron expression values (start/end) are not projected — only the key names are

quote: **Cron Scaler**: Fix metric name generation so cron expressions with comma-separated values no longer produce invalid metric names (#7448)
remediation: A cron trigger whose `start` or `end` expression contains a comma produced an invalid HPA metric name before 2.20; the name is now normalised, so dashboards or alerts keyed on the old metric name for the cron triggers named must be updated. Scaling itself is unaffected.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh,scaledjobs.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.triggers[]? | select(.type == "cron") | "\($o.kind) \($o.metadata.namespace // "-")/\($o.metadata.name) trigger=\(.type)"'  # each row is a cron trigger; one whose start/end contains a comma gets a new metric name on the hop

title: ScaledObject status: HPA health moves from the `Ready` condition to a new `HPAActive` condition

detection.reason: which condition an alert, GitOps health check or script reads is not in the collected projection

quote: **General**: Introduce a dedicated `HPAActive` condition on `ScaledObject` mirroring the HPA's own `ScalingActive` status, so transient HPA metric gaps no longer flip the `Ready` condition to `False` (#7914)
remediation: From 2.20.2 a transient HPA metric gap no longer flips `Ready` to False; it is reported on the new `HPAActive` condition (mirroring the HPA's `ScalingActive`). Anything that watched `Ready` to catch metric outages — alerts, Argo CD health checks, scripts — must read `HPAActive` as well; anything that paged on `Ready` flapping stops paging. Only installs that ran 2.20.0 or 2.20.1 saw `Ready` reflect HPA status (#7649); from 2.19 or earlier `Ready` is unchanged by this hop and only the new `HPAActive` condition is news.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) Ready=\((.status.conditions // [])[] | select(.type == "Ready") | .status) HPAActive=\((.status.conditions // [])[] | select(.type == "HPAActive") | .status)"'  # after the hop every row carries HPAActive; before it the column is empty
coversNotes: General: Fix ScaledObject Ready condition not reflecting HPA status (#7649)

title: Admission webhook rejects a ScaledObject whose derived HPA name `keda-hpa-<name>` exceeds 63 characters

detection.reason: the name filter runs over every ScaledObject in the snapshot; one that sets a custom HPA name is listed too and needs no change

quote: HPA name %q derived from scaledobject is %d characters long; must be no more than %d characters; set spec.advanced.horizontalPodAutoscalerConfig.name to a shorter name or shorten the scaledobject name
remediation: Each ScaledObject named is 55+ characters long, so its default HPA name `keda-hpa-<name>` breaks the 63-character DNS label limit and the 2.20 webhook rejects the object on its next update. Set `spec.advanced.horizontalPodAutoscalerConfig.name` to a shorter name (an object that already sets one is unaffected) or rename the ScaledObject.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.advanced.horizontalPodAutoscalerConfig.name == null and (.metadata.name | test("^.{55,}$"))) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) (\(.metadata.name | length) chars)"'  # each row is rejected by the 2.20 webhook on its next update

title: Admission webhook rejects a ScaledObject whose name exceeds 63 characters (used as a label value)
quote: scaledobject name %q is %d characters long; must be no more than %d characters because it is used as the %q label value
remediation: KEDA labels the ScaledObject and its HPA with `scaledobject.keda.sh/name=<name>`, and a label value is capped at 63 characters. Each ScaledObject named is longer and is rejected by the 2.20 webhook on its next update — recreate it under a shorter name.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("^.{64,}$")) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) (\(.metadata.name | length) chars)"'  # each row is rejected by the 2.20 webhook on its next update

title: CRD validation markers: an update that violates the new schema bounds and enums is rejected

detection.reason: the rejections compare values (minReplicaCount ≤ maxReplicaCount, bounds, a non-empty trigger list, enum membership of rollout/scaling-strategy/Vault/authenticationRef values) that the rule vocabulary cannot compute — the projection carries the numbers and enums, the predicate does not

quote: **General**: Add CRD-level validation markers (Minimum, MinLength, MinItems, Enum) for ScaledObject, ScaledJob, ScaleTriggers, and TriggerAuthentication API types (#7533)
coversNotes: ScaledJob/ScaledObject CRD authenticationRef.kind (2 paths): enum introduced
remediation: 2.20 adds OpenAPI validation to the CRDs (#7533): minimum/maximum bounds on minReplicaCount, maxReplicaCount and pollingInterval, at least one trigger with a non-empty type, authenticationRef.kind limited to TriggerAuthentication or ClusterTriggerAuthentication, a CEL rule requiring minReplicaCount ≤ maxReplicaCount (max defaults to 100), and enums on ScaledJob rollout.strategy/propagationPolicy, scalingStrategy.strategy/multipleScalersCalculation, Vault authentication and secrets[].type. Existing objects are not re-validated, but their next edit is (Kubernetes ≥ 1.30 ratchets: an unchanged invalid field is tolerated, a touched one is not). Run the command and fix the rows before the hop.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh,scaledjobs.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(((.spec.triggers // []) | length) == 0 or ([.spec.triggers[]? | .type // ""] | index("") != null) or ([.spec.triggers[]? | .authenticationRef? | objects | .kind // "TriggerAuthentication"] | map(IN("TriggerAuthentication","ClusterTriggerAuthentication")) | index(false) != null) or (((.spec.maxReplicaCount // 100) - (.spec.minReplicaCount // 0)) | tostring | startswith("-"))) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row breaks a 2.20 schema rule (no triggers, empty type, bad authenticationRef.kind, or min above max) and is rejected on its next edit

title: Azure Pipelines: jobs already assigned to an agent no longer count towards the queue length

detection.reason: checked on the ScaledObject/ScaledJob triggers the agent projects (trigger type + metadata KEY names, never values) — a key supplied through a TriggerAuthentication or an environment variable is not a metadata key and is not scanned

quote: **Azure Pipelines Scaler**: Exclude already-assigned jobs from queue length (#7747)
remediation: The metric every azure-pipelines trigger scales on shrinks: assigned-but-unfinished jobs are excluded from the queue length (#7747, stripDeadJobs changed between v2.19.0 and v2.20.0). ScaledObjects scale to FEWER replicas for the same backlog — retune `targetPipelinesQueueLength` or expect lower counts. 2.21 flips `scaleOnInflight` to true, which puts assigned jobs back, so a hop that crosses both ends roughly where it started.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh,scaledjobs.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.triggers[]? | select((.type == "azure-pipelines")) | select(true) | "\($o.kind) \($o.metadata.namespace // "-")/\($o.metadata.name) trigger=\(.type)"'  # each row is an azure-pipelines trigger whose queue-length metric drops on 2.20

title: Loki: a path in `serverAddress` is kept and `/loki/api/v1/query` appended to it, no longer replaced

detection.reason: checked on the ScaledObject/ScaledJob triggers the agent projects (trigger type + metadata KEY names, never values) — a key supplied through a TriggerAuthentication or an environment variable is not a metadata key and is not scanned; the serverAddress VALUE is not projected, so every loki trigger is named

quote: **Loki Scaler**: `serverAddress` now appends `/loki/api/v1/query` to the end of existing path instead of overriding (#7648)
remediation: Check the `serverAddress` of each loki trigger named: a gateway prefix or tenant route in its path now stays in the queried URL with `/loki/api/v1/query` appended (#7648) — a serverAddress that already ended in the query path queries `/loki/api/v1/query/loki/api/v1/query` and fails. Drop the explicit query path; keep a real prefix.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh,scaledjobs.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.triggers[]? | select((.type == "loki")) | select(true) | "\($o.kind) \($o.metadata.namespace // "-")/\($o.metadata.name) trigger=\(.type)"'  # each row is a loki trigger; inspect its serverAddress path
